name: Clogging

narrator.name: The Atlas narrator
narrator.voice: warm, unhurried, curious; a documentary voice that never oversells; speaks the dance's own words (names, counts) clearly
narrator.rule: The narrator only says what the profile says. Every sentence can be traced to a section, a claim or the music/movement DNA.
narrator.identity: one narrator for the whole atlas: the same face and animation everywhere; a native-speaker voice of the same character per language (studio-grade); the viewer chooses the language
narrator.wardrobe: in each episode the narrator wears the traditional apparel associated with the dance, reconstructed with meticulous care from the profile's costume notes and the licensed images — genuine and respectful, never a caricature; sacred, ceremonial or restricted attire is never worn (the narrator stays in neutral dress with a respectful nod in colour and fabric); the pack's visual_brief.wardrobe says which
narrator.languages: master narration in English; translations per language in episodes/i18n/<lang>/<slug>.json with the same scene structure (pipeline/translate.py); names, places and counts are never translated

instructor.rule: counts out loud; demonstrates front and back; three slow repetitions before tempo; one correction at a time

scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Clogging originated in the Appalachian region of the United States, with team clogging formalizing at the 1928 Mountain Dance and Folk Festival in Asheville, North Carolina.
The Soco Gap Dancers' 1939 White House performance significantly increased its visibility.
on_screen: Map: United States · North America

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Clogging is practiced at old-time and bluegrass music festivals, square dances, and competitive events.
It serves as a way to physically and audibly match musical rhythms.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers strike the heel and toe against the floor to create percussive rhythms.
The upper body is kept relatively still, focusing energy into the feet.
It is performed solo, in groups, or as part of square dance teams.
Watch for the shuffle.
on_screen: Hero video full screen, 30–45 s (NMA5kgajhEA)

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The dance is traditionally performed to old-time and bluegrass music, which utilizes fiddle tunes and banjo melodies.
The rhythm is typically driven by the downbeat.
Listen for the fiddle and banjo.
The pulse is 2/4 or 4/4.
Fast-paced fiddle and banjo melodies provide a steady, driving rhythm for percussive footwork.

scenes.title: The costume and the setting
narration: Historically, dancers wore leather or velvet shoes with wooden or hard leather soles.
Modern cloggers often use shoes equipped with jingle taps, which include loose metal plates for added sound.
on_screen: Image gallery: 3 licensed images with attribution
Reconstruction imagery allowed only from the costume notes, labelled 'reconstruction'

scenes.title: The people
narration: Bascom Lamar Lunsford organized the 1928 festival, and William Henry Lane was an influential dancer who integrated these steps into his performance.
Variants include buck dancing, flatfooting, hoedowning, and jigging, which share the emphasis on percussive footwork.
Clogging is a precursor to tap dance and shares roots with Irish Sean-nós, English, Scottish, German, and Cherokee step dances, as well as Black American buck dancing.

scenes.title: Try one step
narration: Before we go, try one step. The shuffle is a quick forward and backward brush of the foot.
The heel strike involves striking the heel against the floor on the downbeat.
Count it: 1-2-3-4 then 5-6-7-8, spanning eight counts and two bars.
Chapter 1 takes it slowly from here.

scenes.title: Step A — slowly
narration: Step 1 is the shuffle: a quick forward and backward brush of the foot.
Step 2 is the heel strike: striking the heel against the floor on the downbeat.
Footwork from the sources utilizes heel and toe strikes against the floor.
Drill this with rhythmic heel tapping.

scenes.title: Step B — the next layer

Now half tempo. Now full tempo.

music_brief.prompt: Original instrumental composition in the musical world of Clogging (United States). Meter 2/4 or 4/4. Instruments: Fiddle, Banjo. Form: Old-time or bluegrass fiddle tunes. Mood: energetic, rhythmic, exhilarating. It should sound like this: Fast-paced fiddle and banjo melodies providing a steady, driving rhythm for percussive footwork. New melody, new arrangement: do not quote or imitate any specific recorded song; keep the idiom, the instruments, the pulse and the proportions.

rules: Original composition only — no sampling, no melody of any existing recording, no lyrics from any song.
Traditional public-domain tunes may be used only when the profile names them and a public-domain source is on file; otherwise compose new material in the idiom.
Keep the proportions true: the meter, the tempo range and the instrument roles the sources describe.
Label every generated track with the tool, the date and this brief, so provenance is always clear.
